QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_3

question.text: Ganga Infra Trust (a Category I Infrastructure AIF) must circulate annual reports to its investors. By when must the annual report reach LPs?

answer.text: Within 45 days from the year-end, matching mutual-fund disclosure norms.
Within 90 days from the year-end, aligned with the Companies Act audited accounts window.
There is no prescribed timeline for Cat I AIF annual LP reporting.
Within 180 days from the year-end, as stipulated under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations for Category I and II AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations (Regulation 22 and attached disclosure framework) require Category I and II AIFs to provide reports to investors at least annually within 180 days from the year-end, covering investee financials, risk summary, and portfolio commentary. The Trap: 45 days is mutual-fund half-yearly disclosure. 90 days is a Companies Act benchmark. 'No timeline' ignores Regulation 22 specifically. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers this identically. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) uses a 30-day quarterly investor report — do not recycle that number into AIF context. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 180-day window is the OUTER limit. Top-quartile GPs deliver the annual by day-120 because fund-of-funds LPs need it for their own audit cycle. Late reports crater your Fund II fundraise.
